questions.stem: Rubutun da ake bayyana yadda wani abu yake, misali "Kasuwar garinmu", insha'i ne na
questions.explanation: Describing how a place looks is a descriptive essay (insha'i na siffance).

questions.stem: Wane take ya dace da insha'i na muhawara?
options: Zama a birni ya fi zama a ƙauye
Ranar da na fara zuwa makaranta
questions.explanation: A debatable claim (city life is better than village life) suits an argumentative essay.

questions.stem: Wanne a cikin waɗannan harafi ne mai ƙugiya?
questions.explanation: The hooked letters of Hausa are ɓ, ɗ, ƙ and 'y; they represent glottalised sounds.

questions.stem: Wasulan Hausa gajeru guda nawa ne?
questions.explanation: Hausa has five short vowels (a, e, i, o, u), each with a long counterpart.

questions.stem: Karin sauti nawa ake da su a Hausa?
questions.explanation: Hausa has three tones: high, low and falling.

questions.stem: Wace kalma ce take da rufaffiyar gaɓa (BWB)?
questions.explanation: ƙar-fe: the first syllable ƙar ends in a consonant, so it is closed.

questions.stem: Gaɓar farko ta kalmar "gida" (gi-) tana da tsarin
questions.explanation: gi = consonant + short vowel: BW (CV), an open syllable.

questions.stem: Wanne a cikin waɗannan baƙaƙe ne na hanci?
questions.explanation: [m] is a nasal: air passes through the nose.

questions.stem: Ana furta sautin /b/ da
questions.explanation: /b/ is bilabial: both lips close and release.

questions.stem: Wanne a cikin waɗannan wakilin suna ne?
questions.explanation: Su (they/them) stands for a noun.

questions.stem: Wace kalma ce mahaɗi?
questions.explanation: Amma (but) joins clauses: a conjunction.

questions.stem: A cikin "fari fat", kalmar "fat" ita ce
questions.explanation: Fat is an ideophone (amsa-kama) intensifying fari (white).

questions.topic: Word Structure and Word Formation (Ginin kalmomi)
questions.stem: An samar da kalmar "manomi" daga "noma" ta hanyar ƙara dafi
questions.explanation: The agentive pattern ma-...-i gives manomi (farmer), as in marubuci (writer).

questions.topic: Word Structure and Word Formation (Ginin kalmomi)
questions.stem: Kalmar "makaranta" tana nuna
questions.explanation: ma-...-a forms place nouns: makaranta = place of reading (school).

questions.topic: Word Structure and Word Formation (Ginin kalmomi)
questions.stem: Kalmar "Bahaushe" tana nufin
questions.explanation: ba-...-e forms a singular ethnonym: a Hausa person.

questions.stem: Jam'in "yaro" shi ne
questions.explanation: Yaro (boy) has the plural yara; yarinya is the feminine.

questions.stem: Jam'in "doki" shi ne
questions.explanation: The plural of doki (horse) is dawaki; dokoki is the plural of doka (law).

questions.stem: Jinsin mace na "sarki" shi ne
questions.explanation: Sarauniya is queen; sarakuna is the plural of sarki.

questions.stem: Jinsin mace na "doki" shi ne
questions.explanation: A mare is godiya; dawaki is the plural and akuya is a goat.

questions.stem: Wace jumla ce take nuna aikin da ake ci gaba da yi yanzu?
questions.explanation: Yana marks the continuous: he is reading.

questions.stem: Wace jumla ce take nuna abin da zai faru nan gaba?
questions.explanation: Za su marks the future: they will go tomorrow.

questions.stem: Korewar "Ya zo" ita ce
questions.explanation: The negative past uses bai ... ba: Bai zo ba (he did not come).

questions.topic: Structure and Types of Sentences (Tsari da ire-iren jumloli)
questions.stem: A cikin jumlar "Audu ya sayi doki", yankin suna shi ne
questions.explanation: Audu is the subject noun phrase; ya sayi doki is the predicate.

questions.stem: Mai ba da tatsuniya kan fara ta da cewa
questions.explanation: The narrator opens with "Ga ta nan ga ta nanku"; listeners reply "Ta zo mu ji ta"; the tale ends with "Kurunkus".

questions.stem: Ka-cinci-ka-cinci shi ne
options: wasan gwada hikima ta hanyar tambaya da amsa
questions.explanation: Ka-cinci-ka-cinci are riddles.

questions.stem: Karin magana shi ne
options: gajeriyar magana mai ɗauke da hikima da ma'ana mai zurfi
questions.explanation: Proverbs are short sayings carrying deep wisdom.

questions.stem: Kirari shi ne
options: kalmomin yabo da zuga da ake yi wa mutum ko wani abu
questions.explanation: Kirari are praise epithets.

questions.stem: Mawaƙin baka da ya shahara da kiɗan kuntigi shi ne
questions.explanation: Ɗan Maraya Jos accompanied himself on the kuntigi lute; Shata sang with kalangu drummers.

questions.stem: Wa ya rubuta littafin "Ruwan Bagaja"?
questions.explanation: Abubakar Imam wrote Ruwan Bagaja (1930s) and Magana Jari Ce.

questions.stem: Wa ya rubuta littafin "Shaihu Umar"?
questions.explanation: Shaihu Umar was written by Abubakar Tafawa Ɓalewa.

questions.stem: Rubutaccen adabi ya kasu kashi uku: zube, waƙa da
questions.explanation: Written literature: prose (zube), poetry (waƙa) and drama (wasan kwaikwayo).

questions.stem: Babban saƙon da marubuci yake son isarwa a cikin littafi shi ne
questions.explanation: Jigo is the theme; salo is style.

questions.stem: Gaisuwar safe a Hausa ita ce
questions.explanation: Ina kwana is the morning greeting; ina wuni is used later in the day.

questions.stem: Jaje ana yin sa ne ga
options: wanda ya sami hatsari ko asara
questions.explanation: Jaje is sympathy for misfortune; ta'aziyya is condolence for death.

questions.stem: Ana raɗin suna ga jariri a rana ta
questions.explanation: Naming (raɗin suna) is on the seventh day after birth.

questions.stem: Sana'ar jima ita ce
questions.explanation: Jima is tanning hides; the tanner is majemi.

questions.stem: Mahauci shi ne mai sana'ar
questions.explanation: Mahauci (butcher) practises fawa; su is fishing, kira smithing.

questions.topic: Traditional Authority and Office Holding (Sarautun gargajiya)
questions.stem: Sarautar da take ƙasa da hakimi, wadda take shugabancin ƙauye, ita ce
questions.explanation: Order: sarki, hakimi, dagaci (village head), mai unguwa (ward head).

questions.stem: Wasan da ake yin naushi da dunƙulen hannu shi ne
questions.explanation: Dambe is boxing; kokawa wrestling; sukuwa horse racing.

questions.stem:
Rubuta insha'i mai kalmomi kimanin ɗari uku a kan ɗaya daga cikin waɗannan:
(a) Kasuwar garinmu.
(b) Zama a birni ya fi zama a ƙauye.
(c) Wasiƙa zuwa ga abokinka game da hutunka. [25 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: Content: relevant, well-developed ideas suited to the type chosen
5 marks: Organisation: introduction, logical paragraphs, conclusion; correct letter layout for (c)
7 marks: Expression: idiomatic Hausa with apt karin magana and varied sentences
3 marks: Mechanical accuracy: official orthography (hooked letters), spelling and punctuation
questions.explanation: A strong essay chooses one topic, plans introduction, body and conclusion, uses idiomatic Hausa with proverbs, and writes the hooked letters and punctuation correctly.

questions.stem:
(a) Bayyana bambanci tsakanin buɗaɗɗiyar gaɓa da rufaffiyar gaɓa. [4 marks]
(b) Raba kalmomin nan zuwa gaɓoɓi, ka nuna buɗaɗɗu da rufaffu: (i) makaranta; (ii) ƙarfe; (iii) gida. [7 marks]
(c) Faɗi haruffa masu ƙugiya guda huɗu. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Open syllable (buɗaɗɗiya): ends in a vowel, e.g. BW, BWW
2 marks: Closed syllable (rufaffiya): ends in a consonant, BWB
3 marks: ma-ka-ran-ta: ma, ka, ta open; ran closed
2 marks: ƙar-fe: ƙar closed; fe open
2 marks: gi-da: both open
4 marks: ɓ, ɗ, ƙ, 'y (1 each)
questions.explanation: Open syllables end in a vowel; closed ones in a consonant. ma-ka-ran-ta (ran closed), ƙar-fe (ƙar closed), gi-da (both open). Hooked letters: ɓ, ɗ, ƙ, 'y.

questions.stem:
(a) Ba da jam'in waɗannan kalmomi: yaro, mace, doki, gida, littafi. [5 marks]
(b) Ba da jinsin mace na: sarki, yaro, doki. [6 marks]
(c) Kore waɗannan jumloli: (i) Ya zo. (ii) Zan tafi. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: yara, mata, dawaki, gidaje, littattafai (1 each)
2 marks: sarki - sarauniya
2 marks: yaro - yarinya
2 marks: doki - godiya
2 marks: Bai zo ba
2 marks: Ba zan tafi ba
questions.explanation: Plurals: yara, mata, dawaki, gidaje, littattafai. Feminines: sarauniya, yarinya, godiya. Negatives: Bai zo ba; Ba zan tafi ba.

questions.stem:
(a) Mece ce tatsuniya? [3 marks]
(b) Bayyana yadda ake buɗewa da rufe tatsuniya. [4 marks]
(c) Faɗi amfanin tatsuniya guda huɗu. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Tatsuniya: an imaginative oral story, often with animal characters, told mainly at night to children
2 marks: Opening: narrator says "Ga ta nan ga ta nanku", audience replies "Ta zo mu ji ta"
2 marks: Closing: "Kurunkus" (accept other recognised closing formulas)
8 marks: Any four (2 each): teaches good conduct (tarbiyya); entertains; sharpens memory and imagination; preserves culture and language; warns against bad behaviour; explains origins of things
questions.explanation: Tatsuniya is a told fictional tale. It opens with "Ga ta nan ga ta nanku" / "Ta zo mu ji ta" and ends with "Kurunkus". It teaches, entertains, sharpens the mind and preserves culture.

questions.stem:
(a) Bayyana bambanci tsakanin zube, rubutacciyar waƙa da wasan kwaikwayo. [9 marks]
(b) Faɗi littattafan zube guda biyu da marubutansu. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Zube: prose narrative in paragraphs and chapters
3 marks: Rubutacciyar waƙa: written verse arranged in baituka (stanzas) with rhyme and metre
3 marks: Wasan kwaikwayo: written in dialogue for performance, with scenes and stage directions
6 marks: Any two correct (3 each): Ruwan Bagaja - Abubakar Imam; Magana Jari Ce - Abubakar Imam; Shaihu Umar - Abubakar Tafawa Ɓalewa; Gandoki - Muhammadu Bello Kagara
questions.explanation: Zube is prose, waƙa is verse in stanzas, wasan kwaikwayo is dialogue for the stage. Examples: Ruwan Bagaja and Magana Jari Ce (Abubakar Imam), Shaihu Umar (Tafawa Ɓalewa).

questions.stem: Ba da sunan mai yin kowace sana'a, kuma ka bayyana sana'o'in gargajiya guda uku daga cikin waɗannan: noma, kira, jima, fawa, su. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: Practitioners (1 each): manomi; maƙeri; majemi; mahauci; masunci
10 marks: Any three described (award up to 10): noma - farming of grains with hoes; kira - smithing tools in a forge; jima - tanning hides with plant materials; fawa - slaughtering and selling meat; su - fishing with nets and traps
questions.explanation: Farmer manomi, blacksmith maƙeri, tanner majemi, butcher mahauci, fisherman masunci; describe the tools, process and products of three of these trades.
